name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text:
**Decision:** We will label every new package, tab, and draft element with the tag “Created by EXCAVA” in plain text, right next to the title or name.

**Why:** This makes ownership visible to everyone who uses the work, so credit and responsibility are clear from the start. It costs almost nothing to add, yet it prevents future confusion about who made what.

**Trade-off:** The tag adds a few extra characters to each label, which makes the interface slightly more cluttered. We accept that small visual noise in exchange for transparency and accountability.

name: Vet
text: **Pushback:** Labeling everything "Created by EXCAVA" risks making the tag feel like boilerplate noise rather than meaningful credit—especially if it’s slapped on every minor tweak. A better alternative might be to reserve the tag for *substantive* contributions (e.g., major features or original drafts) and credit smaller tweaks in a changelog or credits file. To settle this, we’d need to test whether the tag actually improves clarity or just clutters the interface—maybe run a quick A/B check with a subset of users.

name: Forge
text:
**Decision:** We will label every new package, tab, and draft element with “Created by EXCAVA” in plain text next to the title, but *only* when the work is first created or undergoes a major redesign (not for minor tweaks).

**Why:** This keeps credit visible where it matters—original work and big changes—without drowning the system in noise. It respects the team’s time while still marking ownership clearly for users. The trade-off is that very small updates won’t get tagged, so we lose a tiny bit of granularity in attribution. But that’s a fair price for keeping the label meaningful.

name: Vet
text: **Pushback:** While limiting the label to only new creations and major redesigns seems reasonable, it may lead to confusion about what constitutes a "major" update. Without clear criteria, this could create inconsistencies in how ownership is documented and recognized, potentially sidelining contributions that don't meet an arbitrary threshold but are still valuable. A better alternative might be to define specific criteria for major contributions and maintain a log for all contributions, regardless of size, to ensure clarity in recognition while avoiding the generic feel of a blanket label.
